title: MDKS Measurement Technique IDs and Domain Knowledge
description: Static reference card: catalog of all measurement techniques (instruments/methods) used in ThermoML. Covers 160 standard methods from the controlled vocabulary, 97 custom abbreviation codes with UFactor encoding, and 2,647 unique custom method strings. The agent consults this card to understand WHAT techniques are available, HOW they work, and WHICH property groups they serve. NOT per-paper — this is global domain knowledge about instrumentation.

database_stats.note: Counts from full DB scan of 11,923 papers / 130,104 block_properties entries

cross_group_methods.description: 20 standard methods that serve multiple property groups. These are versatile techniques whose measured quantity depends on the property group context.

items.name: Drop ice or diphenyl ether calorimetry

custom_method_encoding.description: Custom methods (method_type='custom') are free-text strings authored by experimentalists. Two major patterns exist: structured abbreviation codes (often with UFactor suffix) and plain free-text descriptions.

ufactor_pattern.description: Pattern: ABBREV:UFactor:N — where ABBREV is a short code for the technique and N is an integer uncertainty multiplier. Some variants include intermediate qualifiers (e.g., 'VIBTUB:FP:UFactor:4', 'SMALLAD:dCP:0.2:UFactor:2'). The UFactor value scales the base uncertainty of the method.
examples: VIBTUB:UFactor:4  → Vibrating tube method, uncertainty factor 4
CAPTUB:UFactor:2  → Capillary tube viscometry, uncertainty factor 2
SMALLAD:dCP:0.2%:UFactor:2 → Small adiabatic calorimetry with 0.2% Cp uncertainty, factor 2

uncertainty_model.description: How measurement uncertainty is encoded in ThermoML. Tied to the technique used: experimentalists estimate expanded uncertainty for each data point based on their method's error budget.
uncertainty_model.per_datapoint_field: nCombExpandUncertValue — the expanded uncertainty for each data point
uncertainty_model.digits_fields: nPropDigits, nVarDigits, nConstrDigits — significant figures of the reported numeric value
uncertainty_model.ufactor_note: Custom methods with :UFactor:N suffix encode a multiplier on the base uncertainty of the technique abbreviation. Higher N means the author assigned proportionally larger uncertainty.
